Patient demographics:
  age: 63
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: Oceania
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Financial Analyst
  trauma_type: Life-threatening accident
  pcl5: 65

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Olfactory (Smell): Related smells, Darkness: Dark spaces, Auditory (Cars): Car sounds
  Threat: Body Reacts Before Mind: My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think, Waking Alert: I wake during the night to check whether I am safe, Scanning Exits: I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
  Memory: Feels Present Not Past: The memory feels like it is happening right now rather than something that is over, Auditory Recall: When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event., Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
  Negative Appraisals: Hypervigilance: I have to be on guard all the time, Thought Avoidance: If I think about the event, I will not be able to handle it, Constant Vigilance: I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next

Vignette:
Kai'olu had always been a meticulous man, with an eye for detail that served him well in his career as a financial analyst. But it wasn't until the night of the accident, three years ago, that he began to notice the world around him in a different way. He was driving home from work on a dark and stormy evening when another car ran a red light and crashed into his vehicle, sending Kai'olu's car spinning out of control. The smell of burning rubber and shattered glass still lingered in his mind, transporting him back to that chaotic moment whenever he caught a whiff of something similar. The sound of screeching tires and crunching metal echoed in his ears long after the accident had passed, making him wince every time he heard a car drive by too quickly or brake too hard. As Kai'olu slowly pieced together the events of that night, he became increasingly aware of the darkness that seemed to closing in around him. The dark spaces in his home and office began to feel oppressive, as if they were waiting to swallow him whole. His wife, Naomi, would often find him turning on lights in rooms he wasn't even using, just to banish the shadows. At night, Kai'olu's body seemed to be constantly on high alert, waking him with a start whenever he heard an unfamiliar noise or felt a slight movement in the bed. He'd lie awake for hours, his heart racing as he checked and rechecked that all the doors and windows were locked, making sure they were safe from whatever dangers might lurk outside. When he was out and about, Kai'olu found himself scanning every room and building for exits, always on the lookout for potential escape routes. It wasn't just a habit – it felt like an essential survival strategy. His mind would replay the accident over and over, as if searching for clues that might help him prevent something similar from happening again. The memories of that night still felt more like lived experiences than distant recollections. When Kai'olu closed his eyes, he could almost smell the smoke and hear the shattering glass. The sounds were so vivid that he sometimes wondered if they were real or just a product of his own mind. Naomi would try to reassure him, but even she couldn't fully understand why these small triggers set off such a maelstrom of emotions. For Kai'olu, thinking about the accident was like staring into an abyss – it made him feel like he might lose himself forever. He'd tried to push those thoughts away, focusing instead on his work or spending time with Naomi and their family. But the constant vigilance wore him down, making him feel like a soldier on permanent guard duty. As the months went by, Kai'olu started noticing changes in his relationships at work. His colleagues would comment on how jumpy he was, how easily startled. They didn't understand why he needed to take long breaks just to calm himself down or why he insisted on sitting with his back against a solid wall during meetings. Naomi noticed the toll it took on their relationship too – Kai'olu's constant need for reassurance and safety had started to feel suffocating at times. They'd argue about things that seemed insignificant, like whether they should go out for dinner or stay in. But beneath those surface-level disagreements lay a deeper fear: what if something happened again? Kai'olu knew he couldn't keep living like this – constantly on edge, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios. He was starting to feel trapped by his own fears and anxieties. Naomi had finally convinced him to seek help, but as Kai'olu sat in the therapist's office for their first session, he couldn't shake off the feeling that he was already too late – that some deep-seated part of himself had been irreparably broken on that fateful night three years ago. He took a deep breath and began to speak, his voice barely above a whisper: "I just want to feel safe again. I want to be able to walk into a room without thinking about the exits. I want to sleep at night without waking up in terror." As he spoke, Kai'olu felt a glimmer of hope that maybe – just maybe – it wasn't too late for him to learn how to live with himself once more.
